_comment: ONE principle: an agent command must not exhaust the machine that
hosts every other session in the tree.
go test -fuzz with default parallelism spawns one worker per core,
each with unbounded memory. On this machine it reaches ~55 GB RSS in
minutes; the kernel OOM kill then takes down the whole desktop app
cgroup that launched it, every other agent session included.
-fuzztime bounds duration, not workers, so it does not exempt a run.
Seeded smoke runs (go test with no -fuzz flag) are never affected.
Separate from destructive-commands.json on purpose: that file answers
'is this call about to lose work in this tree', this one answers 'is
this call about to starve the whole machine'. They need different
correctiveMessage: go test -fuzz with default parallelism spawns one worker per core with unbounded memory and OOM-kills the session that launched it. Rerun capped: go test -fuzz <Target> -parallel 2 -fuzztime 60s. Seeded smoke runs without -fuzz are always fine.
